exposure: Mode of labor induction (transcervical balloon catheters or prostaglandins)
Number of labor induction methods used
cohort: 882 singleton pregnancies at or after 37 weeks gestation who underwent cesarean section during labor, with 416 having spontaneous labor and 464 undergoing labor induction
finding: Elective labor induction did not increase the risk of cesarean section complications, but using prostaglandins after transcervical balloon catheters was associated with a higher risk of severe postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Women with spontaneous labor had fewer non-emergency cesarean deliveries and more uterine pedicle injuries, but no difference in postpartum hemorrhage compared to those with induced labor.
